item.title: Said & Checked, Louisiana, 2026-11-23: 2 contradicted (John Kennedy)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • John Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “It would mean that 200 million Americans would have to give up their health insurance through their employer and turn to the federal government for all of their health insurance.” Contradicted. The Census Bureau's report for 2024 (P60-288, Table 1) puts employment-based coverage at 181.3 million people, about 19 million below 200 million; that count includes dependents and anyone covered at any point in the year, so a point-in-time count would be lower. The 2025 figure is not yet published, which is what remains open.
  • John Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “I’ve saved up about $30 million.” Contradicted. AskAmerica's FEC data show John Kennedy for US with $19.53 million cash on hand at the end of its latest report (through Sept. 30, 2026), and the FEC's candidate totals give the same figure; total receipts since January 2023 are $27.5 million. What remains open: reports after Sept. 30 are not yet filed, and money held outside the campaign committee was not checked.

item.title: Said & Checked, Louisiana, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Markwayne Mullin, Bennie Thompson)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “I was meeting the governor there.” Unsettled. No schedule or statement from Gov. Jeff Landry's office and no report of a meeting at the game was found; reports place Mullin in a private box with tickets obtained through Rep. Steve Scalise. The record neither shows a meeting nor shows that none was planned.
  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “Reported as: Mullin had said Tuesday and reiterated Wednesday that he is required to fly on government planes and that he personally paid for the trip.” Unsettled. DHS told CNN that Mullin was "required by law" to use a government plane and pays personally for non-official flights, but no statute or DHS policy text and no payment or reimbursement record was found. The claim rests only on Mullin's and DHS's own statements.
  • Bennie Thompson, U.S. Representative from Mississippi: “While Americans were stranded in airports across the country, with many sleeping on the floor at their gates, the secretary boarded a luxury jet, flew to a college football game.” Unsettled. The AP reports Mullin flew on a government plane to the LSU-Texas game on Saturday, Nov. 14, the day after the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop, which the AP says ended around 8:15 p.m. ET Friday. AskAmerica's FAA advisory data show airport-level ground stops continuing at some airports on Nov. 14 and 15, but neither source shows whether passengers were still stranded when the flight left.

item.title: Said & Checked, Louisiana, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 6 unsettled (Bill Cassidy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Bill Cassidy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “So, I'm in regular contact with the CDC director.” Unsupported. No page that could be read shows how often the senator and the CDC director are in contact. The search covered web searches on the two and the warehouse catalog, which holds no record of contacts between members and officials.
  • Bill Cassidy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “And then she texted back to say it's been broken for a year. And so she's working to fix it.” Unsupported. No page that could be read says how long the federal flu-shot locator was broken or records the CDC director's reply. The search covered the vaccine locator site, the flu-shot locator and the CDC director; an NBC News page on the subject failed to load.
  • Bill Cassidy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “He was supposed to be doing something positive on ultra-processed foods. That's what MAHA moms wanted. There's been minimal progress.” Unsettled. A trade outlet, Food Industry Executive, reported that the FDA and the health department sent a proposed definition of ultra-processed food to the White House budget office in August 2026 as a white paper, not a rule. No final rule, standard or definition was found, but the submission itself was not read, and "minimal progress" is a judgment the record cannot settle exactly.
